# Persist link mappings with a hit counter

Stores the `code -> target URL` mapping alongside a hit counter and creation
timestamp, so redirects survive restarts and analytics has something to read.

## Operations

1. `create(code, target)` — insert; fail loudly on a duplicate code.
2. `resolve(code)` — return the target or `None`.
3. `bump(code)` — atomically increment the hit counter.

## Table

| Column       | Type    | Notes                          |
| ------------ | ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `code`       | TEXT    | Primary key, from `codec`      |
| `target`     | TEXT    | Absolute http(s) URL           |
| `hits`       | INTEGER | Default 0, bumped per redirect |
| `created_at` | TEXT    | ISO-8601 UTC                   |

## Reference

```python
from snip.store import LinkStore

store = LinkStore.open("snip.db")
store.create("a7Kd93Q", "https://example.com/a/very/long/path")
assert store.resolve("a7Kd93Q") == "https://example.com/a/very/long/path"
store.bump("a7Kd93Q")
```

The counter uses a single `UPDATE ... SET hits = hits + 1` so concurrent redirects
never lose a count[^atomic].

[^atomic]: A read-modify-write in Python would race under the single-writer model;
    pushing the increment into SQL keeps it atomic without an application lock.
